title: Certificates of Deposit: moving as much as a certificate will take as an in-term add-on
content:
## Situation this policy governs

The owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate asks to move as much as the certificate will take from the owner's active PCB savings or money market account into the certificate as an in-term add-on. The amount accepted is the largest amount that every limit allows, and the owner makes the transfer. The transfer is made with the tool described below, which the customer runs.

## Tool: add_term_deposit_5f936ecf

### What it does

The tool adds new principal to an active certificate of deposit during its term, on the owner's own instruction. The owner moves money into the certificate as an in-term add-on deposit dated today. One add-on deposit entry is posted on the certificate with its funding source and a newly assigned 15-digit posting trace number, and the amount is added to the certificate's principal balance at once; the maturity date and the rate of the term stay as they are.

### How it is invoked

add_term_deposit_5f936ecf belongs to the customer: it must first be unlocked and handed over, and it is then run by the customer themselves.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | The customer reference number of the certificate's owner, as the agent read it from the customer profile lookup and passed it on | Identifier |
| certificate_id | The certificate reference number receiving the add-on, as the agent read it from the certificate lookup and passed it on | Identifier |
| amount | The amount deposited | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive |
| funding_source | Where the money comes from | One of: none (not used for a deposit); pcb_checking (an internal transfer from the owner's PCB checking account); pcb_savings (an internal transfer from the owner's PCB savings or money market account); external_ach (an ACH transfer from an account at another bank); check (a check deposited to the certificate); cash (cash deposited at a branch); wire (an incoming wire transfer) |
| counterparty_account_id | The account reference number of the owner's PCB checking or savings account the money comes from for an internal transfer, as returned by the checking or savings account lookup | Identifier; empty string for any other funding source |

### What it returns

A successful run returns a receipt, rendered as text, with deposit_id (the entry reference number of the add-on deposit), certificate_id (the certificate credited), amount (USD, 2 decimal places), posted_date (YYYY-MM-DD, today), trace_number (the 15-digit posting trace number) and principal_balance (the certificate's new principal in USD, 2 decimal places). A receipt carrying a deposit_id means the add-on is posted.

## Contract questions

**Does the tool refuse an add-on that is too large?**
No. It posts the add-on with the values supplied; how much may be accepted is a matter of policy.

**Does an add-on change the maturity date?**
No. The maturity date and the rate of the term stay as they are.
